Domain 3 · corrected replication

Figure 6, rebuilt on the test corner

The published panels score Marformer on every missing cell in the graph while Stan is scored on the 414-cell corner. Rebuilt on the corner for both arms, with the non-transductive curve extended to the full item sweep and the published Stan curves overlaid.

What changed since these panels were drawn

September update · three items, one of which changes the figure

1. Stan now has measurements past K=500. The paper stops the Stan curve at 500 for HMC cost and draws it flat beyond; the tabs to the left reproduce that flat line as a dotted reference, not a measurement. Stan Proj and Stan Both have since been fit out to K=4000 on both draws. Stan does not flatten — Proj keeps improving all the way out, so the flat extension understated it.

2. The gap is the stable quantity; the level is not. The absolute corner log-loss moves ~0.08 nats between generative draws, which is the entire measured draw-to-draw sd. The Marformer−Stan difference moves 0.001–0.02 at K ≥ 1000. A hard draw is hard for both models, so the draw effect is common-mode and cancels.

3. The epoch fix closes about a sixth of the gap. F13 (raised cap, per-run carve selection, refit) is worth 0.0022 nats at K=1000 and 0.0228 at K=4000, against a K=4000 gap of 0.126. It is worth having and it is not the answer. An earlier version of this panel said the fix "lands where Stan is not drawn" — true only while Oracle stopped at K=500 in our scoring, which was the bookkeeping error described above. Oracle runs to K=4000, so F13's gains sit squarely inside the compared region.

Does a terminal learning-rate decay buy anything?

The shipped configuration trains at a flat 2e-4 for its whole budget ("lr_schedule": "none"). Every finished run's final checkpoint was copied to an isolated tree and resumed — weights and AdamW moments — for a short decay phase, against a control that continues at the flat rate for exactly the same number of extra steps. Without that control the comparison is unreadable: the annealed arm has also had more training, and that alone moves the metric.

Terminal cosine decay vs continuing at the flat lr, 100 extra epochs from the same checkpoint and the same AdamW state

The two metrics disagree, and that is the result. On the quiet whole-graph metric the schedule is worth 0.013 at K=500 and nothing (≤0.003) at K ≥ 1000. On the corner — what the paper reports — the sign flips across sizes and every value sits inside the 0.035 paired between-arm sd measured in Part 0. An effect visible only in the metric we do not report, at a magnitude the metric we do report cannot resolve, is not an effect to ship. The epoch budget (F13) already collects what there is to collect here.

What each method cost to fit — temporary, rough

Treat every number here as an order of magnitude, not a measurement. These are elapsed_seconds and fit_elapsed_seconds scraped from the launcher metadata of runs submitted for other purposes, on a shared cluster, n=1, with no control over node contention. Draw 105's Stan Oracle is slower at K=3000 than at K=4000, which is not a property of the model. The paper's runtime figure needs a controlled pass.

Two asymmetries are deliberate and stated rather than hidden. Different hardware: Marformer gets a GPU and Stan does not, because HMC here is CPU-only — that is the comparison being made ("what does this curve cost to produce"), not a per-core one. Different work: every Stan fit here is one chain. The final run moves to 4 chains and 2000 sampling iterations, so these are a lower bound on the shipped configuration.

At K=4000, the largest size both families share
methodhardwaredraw 101 (min)draw 105 (min) vs Marformer (T)
Marformer (T)1x H100 + 8 CPU cores37401.0x
Marformer NT1x H100 + 8 CPU cores37401.0x
Stan Oracle8 CPU cores, no GPU75780320.4x
Stan Bin8 CPU cores, no GPU1101443.0x
Stan Proj8 CPU cores, no GPU27460.7x
Stan Both8 CPU cores, no GPU26270.7x

The headline is real but narrower than it looks. Against Stan Oracle — the well-specified model, the one the gap is measured against — Marformer is ~20x faster at K=4000 (37 min against 12.6 hours), and the ratio grows with K. Against the misspecified Stan variants it is not: Proj and Both fit in 26–27 minutes, comparable to Marformer or better. So the amortisation argument should be made against the model that is actually competitive on accuracy, not against Stan in general.

One thing to check before the paper goes out

The appendix says Stan Oracle is fit with 4 chains and 500 sampling iterations each, for 2000 post-warmup draws, and reports split-R̂. The runner in this repository defaults to CHAINS=1, nothing in the harness overrides it, and every Stan run directory on both draws contains exactly one draw CSV. So the runs behind the curves above are 1 chain, 300 warmup, 500 sampling — which is also why split-R̂ is what got reported: with one chain it is the only R̂ available.

Refits with 4 chains have since been done at K=1000 and K=4000. The predictive number is safe: K=4000 gives 0.6190 / 0.6178 / 0.6180 across 1-chain, 4-chain, and 4-chain-with-long-warmup — 0.0012 nats across an eightfold range of draws. But between-chain R̂ on lp__ is 1.12 at both sizes at the shipped budget, and sigma_uit reaches 1.58 at K=4000; a longer warmup brings lp__ to 1.03 and sigma_uit to 1.11. One chain could not have shown any of this.

Whoever wrote the appendix should confirm what the original seed-42 fits actually ran, since those results did not survive the migration and cannot be inspected here.

What changed

Two corrections · one extension

1. The evaluation set (D22/D23). test.py builds train_obs + test_obs + test_miss + train_miss and averages every missing token, while Stan is scored on missing_ratings_indexes_in_test_instance alone. The paper says the corner is the target: “All reported log-losses are evaluated on missing entries within this corner.” At K=4000 only 2.9% of the published Marformer number is corner.

2. Checkpoint selection (D14). Published points are an argmin over ~18 checkpoints scored on test. These use block-validation: carve, select the stopping epoch on the carve, refit on the whole training partition. Test is never consulted and the refit’s data budget equals Stan’s.

3. The NT curve now spans the full sweep — it stopped at K=900, and the plot script capped it at 500, while the transductive arm ran to 4000.

On the Stan curves. No Domain 3 sigmoid Stan results survived the migration, so these are read by eye off the published figures rather than recomputed — roughly ±0.005 nats. They need no correction: Stan was always scored on the corner, which is why overlaying them here is apples-to-apples and the published figure was not. Beyond K=500 on the item axis the paper draws Stan flat for cost reasons; that is reproduced as a dotted reference, not a measurement.

Three things to know before quoting these

Caveats that change how the panels should be read

  • The error bars understate the uncertainty (D27). The bands are the standard deviation across 3 seeds (~±0.01). The corner is a fixed 414 cells, so any measurement carries about ±0.06 at 95% from cell sampling, and more seeds cannot reduce it because every seed scores the same cells. Point-to-point moves under 0.06 are not signal. This is a deliberate paired design — a fixed hard corner lowers comparison variance — but the reported error bar should be a bootstrap over cells, not a seed sd.
  • The spike at K=600 is a chunking artifact (D24), not the model. It lands exactly where the graph first needs a second chunk at max_item=300. Raising the chunk size to 500 moved it to K=900 rather than removing it. The actual fix is to keep the corner whole and in a chunk that carries training context, which is what these panels now do — it removes the spike and the apparent NT divergence together.
  • CORRECTED — the non-transductive arm does not diverge. An earlier version of this page reported NT degrading badly past K=900 (1.13 at K=4000). That was an evaluation artifact: the corner is always the highest item ids, so contiguous chunking put 239 of its 414 cells in a 36-item orphan chunk containing zero training items, where they scored 1.29 against 0.86 for the cells that kept context. Evaluating with the corner held in one chunk with training context, NT tracks the transductive arm within ±0.03 at every size (0.8673 vs 0.8616 at K=4000). The same fix removes the K=600 spike in the transductive curve (1.0934 → 0.9207); both were the same root cause. The paper’s claim that NT is “comparable at large training sizes” holds.

Added September: what happens past K=4000

The 10k pilot · a different generative draw · corner-scored

This is not an extension of the curves above. The pilot has its own generative draw and therefore its own corner, and D28 measured 0.085 nats of draw-to-draw movement in the absolute level — most of any effect worth looking for. Its numbers cannot be read against seed 42's. What can be compared across draws is the shape, which is what panel (b) shows: every curve shifted to its own K=1000, so the draw offset cancels and only the slope survives.

The pilot also runs at max_item=300 throughout. The max_item=600 arm exists only to K=4000 — it dies at K=6000 with a CUDA OOM, 78.4 GiB in use on an 80 GB H100, because activation memory scales with the number of chunks as well as their width. The shipped chunk size is what makes a 10k run possible at all.
